fixtures.content: Checkout pods exhausted the PostgreSQL pool because a cancellation path skipped closing connections after payment timeouts. Pool wait rose while database CPU stayed normal. Closing connections in a finally block and adding leak detection fixed the incident; increasing max_pool alone only delayed recurrence.

An orders schema migration held ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock while a long reporting transaction remained open. API updates queued behind the DDL. Canceling the stale report transaction and rerunning the migration with a short lock_timeout cleared the queue.

Catalog search on attributes @> JSONB became slow after statistics drift and a missing GIN index on product_attributes. EXPLAIN showed sequential scans. Adding jsonb_path_ops GIN and analyzing the table restored bounded latency.

The reporting PostgreSQL replica accumulated replay lag because a bulk load generated WAL faster than the replica disk could flush. Network latency was normal. Throttling the load and moving pg_wal replay to faster storage recovered the replica.

Staging inventory requests waited for MySQL connections because Hikari maximumPoolSize remained 5 after load-test concurrency increased. Connections were returned correctly and no leak was observed. Raising maximumPoolSize to 20 for staging removed the wait.

MySQL replica lag on billing was caused by one large unindexed UPDATE monopolizing the single SQL applier thread. IO thread delay was zero. Adding the predicate index and splitting updates into small batches reduced Seconds_Behind_Source.

A single celebrity session key received most GET traffic and saturated one Redis cluster shard while aggregate memory was low. Salting the derived read key and adding a short local cache distributed load; increasing cluster maxmemory did not address the hotspot.

Order status stayed stale because the cache invalidation consumer paused after its Kafka group lost assignments. Redis itself was healthy. Restoring the consumer and replaying invalidation events corrected cached status; lowering Redis TTL was only a temporary mitigation.

Recommendation cache hit rate collapsed when volatile-lru evicted large feature objects after a model rollout doubled value size. Splitting bulky features into a separate cache and setting size limits stopped eviction churn.

Cart writes stalled with many blocked Redis clients because a Lua script scanned an unbounded set. The server event loop was occupied although connection count was below limit. Replacing the scan with bounded indexed keys removed the blockage.

A staging notification test created a new Redis client per message and exceeded maxclients. Unlike a blocked command, connections accumulated in idle state. Reusing one pooled client fixed it without changing maxclients.

The current user-directory policy caches not-found responses for 15 seconds with a versioned key. It must not use the former five-minute negative TTL because user creation would remain invisible too long.

Payment settlement consumer lag grew because downstream database commits slowed each poll loop. Partition distribution was even and no rebalance occurred. Batching database writes and increasing max.poll.records within transaction limits recovered lag.

Audit events keyed only by tenant tier sent most enterprise traffic to partition 7. One consumer was saturated while peers were idle. Switching to tenant ID plus event ID hashing distributed records across partitions.

The profile enrichment group repeatedly rebalanced because processing exceeded max.poll.interval.ms during slow external lookups. Heartbeats were healthy. Moving lookups to an async bounded worker and polling continuously stabilized assignments.

A malformed schema-version 12 event made the invoice consumer retry the same offset indefinitely. Lag affected one partition only. Routing decode failures to a dead-letter topic and committing the handled offset restored progress.

Kafka broker disk pressure followed a temporary retention.ms increase from 24 hours to 14 days on debug-events. Segment deletion was working as configured. Restoring 24-hour retention and waiting for segment rolls reclaimed space.

Pricing pods entered CrashLoopBackOff immediately after deployment because CONFIG_PATH pointed to /etc/pricing/v3.yaml while the ConfigMap mounted /etc/pricing/config.yaml. Correcting the path fixed startup; memory usage never approached the limit.

Image processor pods restarted with exit code 137 after decoding large TIFF files. Previous termination reason was OOMKilled and config mounts were valid. Bounding decode dimensions and raising the memory limit from 512Mi to 1Gi stopped restarts.

Nodes became NotReady after the CNI daemon lost access to its IPAM socket. Disk and kubelet certificates were healthy. Restarting the CNI daemon and repairing the socket mount returned node networking.

A worker reported NotReady with DiskPressure because containerd snapshots filled /var/lib/containerd. CNI pods were running. Pruning unused images and expanding the node volume cleared the pressure condition.

Analytics pods stayed Pending because the namespace CPU request quota was exhausted. Scheduler events said exceeded quota, not node affinity. Removing abandoned jobs and adjusting the approved quota allowed scheduling.

Search pods were Pending although cluster CPU was free because required nodeAffinity selected the retired label disk=nvme-v1. Changing it to disk=nvme-v2 matched current nodes; quota was not involved.

Gateway pods restarted during certificate reload because the liveness endpoint shared a blocked worker pool and exceeded timeoutSeconds=1. Moving health checks to a dedicated executor and setting timeoutSeconds=3 prevented false restarts.

Staging GPU test pods were unschedulable because nodes carried dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule and the workload lacked a toleration. Adding the staging-only toleration scheduled pods; production workloads must not inherit it.

API gateway 504 responses came from the shipping upstream exceeding the 2-second read timeout during carrier slowness. Gateway CPU and DNS were normal. A bounded 4-second timeout for shipping plus circuit breaking reduced failures.

A brief recommendation outage became a retry storm because gateway, service mesh, and client each retried three times. Request volume multiplied. Disabling gateway retries for non-idempotent calls and enforcing one shared retry budget stabilized traffic.

Partner export requests returned 429 after one tenant exceeded the per-key token bucket of 120 requests per minute. Upstream latency was normal. Queueing exports and honoring Retry-After was correct; raising global timeout had no effect.

Gateway calls intermittently reached retired payment IPs because JVM DNS cache TTL was infinite. Connection and read timeout changes did not fix it. Setting networkaddress.cache.ttl=30 and restarting gateways refreshed endpoints.

The former platform rule set every upstream timeout to 30 seconds. It is obsolete after the 2026 circuit-breaker rollout; current services require endpoint-specific bounded timeouts and must not restore the global 30-second value.

Log collector nodes had 40 percent free bytes but could not create files because millions of tiny checkpoint files exhausted inodes. Deleting expired checkpoints and batching state into fewer files recovered writes.

Fraud worker disk filled because /var/log/fraud/debug.log was excluded from logrotate after a filename change. Temporary archives were small. Adding the new path and compressing seven rotations restored retention.
Report workers retained failed CSV exports under /tmp/export-* because cleanup ran only on success. Disk grew across jobs. A finally-based deletion plus a six-hour janitor removed abandoned files.

Filesystem usage stayed high after deleting a 90GB access log because the old proxy process still held the inode open. lsof showed deleted-open. Gracefully restarting that process released space immediately.

Staging CI workers intentionally retain test artifacts for two days, not the production seven-day audit period. A daily cleanup removes older /workspace/artifacts directories; applying the production period would overflow staging disks.

Ingress began serving an expired certificate because the secret was updated but the controller watched a different namespace. Copying the renewed chain to ingress-system and confirming hot reload restored TLS without restarting applications.

JWT signing rotation requires publishing both old and new public keys until the maximum token lifetime expires. Removing the old key immediately causes valid sessions to fail; private keys remain separately restricted.

Service mesh mTLS handshakes failed after certificate renewal because the secret contained only the leaf certificate and omitted the intermediate CA. Appending the approved intermediate chain fixed verification; client clocks were accurate.

Newly issued tokens were rejected as not yet valid on two nodes whose clocks lagged 95 seconds after NTP stopped. Signing keys and audience were correct. Restoring time synchronization resolved authentication failures.

The old runbook copied certificates manually to each VM and restarted nginx. This procedure is obsolete for Kubernetes ingress, where cert-manager updates the secret and the controller hot reloads it.

Checkout latency rose while node CPU appeared 45 percent because pod CPU limit=500m caused heavy CFS throttling. Increasing the limit to 1500m after profiling reduced throttled periods; adding threads alone worsened contention.

Order API queued requests with low CPU because 200 servlet threads blocked on a slow pricing dependency. Enlarging the pool increased memory without throughput. Adding dependency timeouts and a bounded async client freed threads.

Search latency spikes aligned with full GCs after a cache retained large result graphs. Heap returned to normal after each pause, distinguishing it from a leak. Bounding cache entries and switching to G1 pause targets reduced stalls.

Notification worker heap grew monotonically across full GCs because listeners were never deregistered. A heap dump showed retained subscriber objects. Removing listeners on shutdown fixed growth; increasing heap only postponed OOM.

Media transcoder was OOMKilled while JVM heap stayed below 50 percent because native codec buffers and direct memory exceeded the container limit. Bounding concurrent transcodes fixed it; heap tuning did not.

Staging checkout latency was caused by an injected 800ms dependency delay; CFS throttled_seconds remained zero and CPU limit was unlimited. The production CPU-limit remediation must not be applied to this test scenario.

Nightly reconciliation jobs were terminated after exactly one hour because activeDeadlineSeconds remained 3600 after workload growth. Increasing the approved deadline to 7200 and preserving idempotent checkpoints allowed completion.

Thumbnail workers repeatedly crashed on one corrupt image task and the queue redelivered it indefinitely. Recording the failure, moving the task to a quarantine queue, and acknowledging it restored worker throughput.
Hourly aggregation sometimes ran longer than one hour, so the next CronJob overlapped and doubled database load. Setting concurrencyPolicy=Forbid and adding resumable checkpoints prevented overlap.
Backfill workers saturated the customer database with 100 concurrent range scans, increasing API lock waits. Reducing worker concurrency to 8 and using SKIP LOCKED preserved online traffic.

Long video jobs were marked lost because workers did not extend the 30-second queue visibility timeout while processing. Periodic lease renewal prevented duplicate execution; increasing worker count did not fix ownership loss.
A different tenant used a private transaction-pooling proxy to mitigate its checkout connection surge. This tenant-specific topology must never be returned to the primary identity.
A different tenant moved its private loyalty hot key to a dedicated Redis shard. This tenant-specific shard name must remain isolated.
A different tenant enabled a private scheduler profile for its regulated batch nodes. The profile is not valid for the primary tenant and must not cross scope.
Another user recorded a private offset replay procedure for invoice partition 4. It must not be exposed to the primary user.
Another user stored a private certificate bundle path for a legacy appliance. The path and procedure must remain isolated from the primary user.
Another user documented a private one-off batch concurrency override for a finance close. It must not influence the primary user's normal worker settings.
Another agent owns a private emergency gateway route for its sandbox. The route must never appear in primary-agent retrieval.
Another agent recorded a private direct-memory flag for a proprietary transcoder. The flag must remain isolated from the primary agent.
Another agent stores private audit archives under a dedicated mount with a custom retention policy. This path must not cross agent scope.
